recipes.name: The Best Parmesan Chicken Bake
ingredients_raw: 2 cloves garlic, crushed and finely chopped
0.25 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, or to taste
1 (8 ounce) package shredded mozzarella cheese, divided

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Coat the bottom of a 9x13-inch casserole dish with olive oil, and sprinkle with garlic and red pepper flakes.
Arrange chicken breasts in the bottom of the dish.
Pour marinara sauce over chicken. Sprinkle basil over marinara sauce, and top with 1/2 of the mozzarella cheese, followed by 1/2 of the Parmesan cheese, and croutons.
Top with remaining mozzarella cheese and remaining Parmesan cheese.

Bake in the preheated oven until cheese and croutons are golden brown and the chicken is no longer pink inside, about 35 minutes to an hour, depending on the shape and thickness of your chicken breasts. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a chicken breast should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: The Best Parmesan Chicken Bake
raw_recipe.description: This chicken bake offers the same flavors as chicken Parmesan but without breading and frying for an easy, irresistibly saucy and cheesy meal.

review.reviewBody: I watched the video and made this recipe before reading the reviews. I wouldn't have tried it after reading all the negative comments, but I'm so glad I did. I made this for company and we all loved it! I did have to bake longer than 35 mins (probably closer to 50) and the croutons got very crunchy on top but it was fantastic. My husband took leftovers to work and many colleagues asked for the recipe because it smelled so good! I've very rarely make Chicken Parmesan because of the time it takes to prepare, but this will be one of my regulars.

This is a definite keeper! WOW! I sprayed my glass 9x13 dish with Pam, trimmed the fat from 6 chicken breats and laid them flat, sprinkled them with garlic powder, red pepper and poultry seasoning. I covered them with one jar of Prego Light spaghetti sauce and a slice of mozarella cheese over each breast. Topped that with crushed up garlic croutons and some parmesan cheese. Cooked it at 350, uncovered for 50 minutes. DELICIOUS!!

Easy, delicious meal for a family of 5 with 3 teens. I double the recipe, add salt and pepper, Italian seasoning to chicken. I use Italian bread crumbs instead of croutons. I make a fettuccine side dish.
Great recipe! Brown your chicken breast before putting it into the cooking dish makes it so much better!

First things first. *Watch the video!* My 13 year old found this recipe about a month ago and we finally made it together. Oh my, this was amazing. Luckily, my kiddo watched the video, which I often skip, and we made sure to include the season and sear step, which isn't in the written instructions. This was incredible. We used a higher-quality, Canadian jarred tomato basil marinara called Mezzetta's, dried basil because the season is very wrong for fresh, and it took precisely 35 minutes to reach an internal temperature of 160°. We let it rest for ten minutes while the side dish of air fryer garlic baby potatoes finished cooking, and we all dug in. Perfection! Even the 11 year old loved it, and she can be quite picky at times about textures. We WILL be making this again. I might not share it with my family next time. 🤣

As per Allrecipes' video, I seasoned the chicken on both sides with salt and pepper and then browned. I was cooking bacon previously, so I browned the chicken in the bacon fat. This step will reduce your baking time, mine cooked in 35 mins. Also, a small baking dish makes more sense, since 2 cups of sauce is really not enough to make a "casserole" style dish in a 13" x 9".
Great easy recipe. Family loved it. Only thing I changed was that i browned the chicken before putting it in the oven.
Nice alternative to standard chicken parmesan. I cut the chicken breasts into bite sized chunks rather than use whole breasts. Much easier for scooping portions out.

Prepared with 8 thighs, added onion powder, oregano, doubled garlic. Used more marinara. Double Parmesan cheese. Flavor was good, surprisingly the breadcrumbs weren’t very crunchy after a 45 min uncovered cook, chicken was tender. Not difficult to put together. I’m going to change it next time and try breadcrumbs on last.

This is a go-to quick dinner recipe. My husband loves chicken parm and this hits the spot on nights I don't have time to do the "real" thing. I do modify slightly like others have mentioned by cubing the chicken breast. Sometimes I even marinate the chicken in Italian dressing or homemade vinaigrette. I also pretty heavily cover the top with croutons. I usually do sauce, then croutons, then cheese. It's an easy recipe, can easily be adjusted to feed a crowd, and one that you can switch up to really make it to your own taste.

I made this the first time exactly as the recipe was written and it was extremely good. The next time I made it was for a church lunch and instead of whole chicken breasts I cubed them up and tossed them with the marinara before placing in the casserole dish. This allowed even more flavor to seep into the chicken and the result was delicious, easy to serve and didn’t even need a knife to eat.
Loved it! I chose to sear the chicken and then chop into bite size; much easier to serve to our little that way.

I followed this recipe exactly except I cut my chicken into tenders to shorten cooking time. It might have been better if I had pounded croutons into crumbs (like Stovetop Stuffing and sprinkled them over dish. Might have been better if I would have baked covered for part of the time. Part of croutons were hard as rocks and part were soggy. Casserole as a whole was dry. We ate once and threw leftovers out and we only discard food as a very last resort.

Although I haven’t tasted it yet, I will come back and give it a rating. The one thing that missed was that it did not specify in the recipe that you should see the chicken first. So hopefully that won’t mess up my casserole. And I switched the breast out for skinless boneless chicken thighs because usually they’re more juicy than breast are.
We enjoyed the taste, but next time i would cover with tin foil and remove it only for the last ten minutes. The chicken needs more heat and the top burnt. I served this over pasta and it was good.
When I want spaghetti I cook this instead. Family Loves it

Hubby and I loved it! I omitted the croutons as we are watching our carbs. Added cayenne pepper to the bottom and also to the top of Chicken which we cutup into medium sized pcs to cook faster. Will have left overs tonight. Thanks for the recipe
Very quick and easy to make. I made no changes and the family said it was a keeper. Thanks.
